rationale: The primary abstract reports favorable aggregate motor performance with oral tea polyphenols in MPTP monkeys. The cited review describes green-tea polyphenols. A distinct bradykinesia contrast, analyzed counts and a brewed black-tea preparation remain unverified.

Regular and decaffeinated brewed coffee were compared in 26 healthy genetic-subgroup participants. The Karolinska sleepiness day-by-group interaction was p=.001, with no detected day-specific group difference. Attention and imaging outcomes do not measure Parkinson fatigue. Reuse the registered study family for the overlapping imaging reports.
Injected isolated curcumin favored general activity and motor performance in an inflammatory rat model. No passive-resistance outcome is present in the abstract.

The abstract reports general activity, rotarod, beam and grid performance changes. It gives no separate movement-speed comparison. Isolated injected curcumin differs from the frozen culinary preparation.
